title: Every key dot can be clicked to pick it and Backspace deletes it
goal: Any dot that stands for a key, on a property lane in the timeline, on the clip's key line, in a value graph, or on the motion path drawn on the canvas, picks on a click (highlighted so the person can see it), and Backspace or Delete removes the picked keys. Today clicking the dots does not pick them, so a key cannot be removed that way.
notes:
User's words (2026-10-12): "i click on any of these dots and cant select them. want to be able to select, hit backspace and have the point disappear". No screenshot came through; from the conversation (3D keying, graphs, key overlays) 'these dots' are key dots, so the task covers every surface that draws them.

Suspect from code reading, not confirmed: KeyLanesView.swift key glyph (:410-430) has .gesture(keyDrag(...)) BEFORE .onTapGesture; a DragGesture with minimumDistance 0 in the same file (:466) would take every press and the tap never fires. Check which drag keyDrag is and make tap and drag coexist (minimumDistance > 0 for the drag, or a single gesture that decides on release). Delete of keys: EditorCommands.swift:720-737 only when onTimeline && canDeletePickedKeys; EditorCanvasSurface.swift:179 deletes picked keys from the canvas when keySelection.layerID matches; canDeletePickedKeys at EditorState+KeyLanes.swift:207. Related queued: the graph editor task (the-value-graph-lets-you-add-points-pick-the-seg) and the key overlay task (clicking-a-key-opens-the-same-overlay-to-set-tha) build on picking working.
acceptance: Reproduce first at Next defaults: key a layer's position, scale, opacity and Rotation Y; click each kind of dot (lane keys, the clip's summary key line, graph points with Show Graph, motion path dots on the canvas) and record which pick and which do not, and what Backspace does after each

A single click on any key dot picks it within one frame with a clear picked look (filled, accent colour, slightly larger); Shift or Command adds; clicking empty lane space drops the pick; a press that moves past the drag threshold still drags the key as today (click and drag must not steal each other)

Backspace and Delete remove the picked keys in one undo step from wherever the pick was made (timeline, graph or canvas), regardless of which pane last had focus, as long as keys are the current pick; the menu bar's Delete shows it is acting on keys
Right-click on a dot picks it (if not already) and offers Delete Key, easing, Copy/Paste
Same rule for every property, including the 3D ones and camera values
A walk keys four properties, clicks a dot on each surface, presses Backspace, and checks the key is gone and the others are untouched
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

On a key lane and the clip key line, the same rule as the value graph and the sound volume line, one implementation shared by all three: One shared rule for every animated line on the timeline (the user, 2026-10-13): a single click on a dot picks it, a single click on the line between two dots picks that segment, and only a double click or a Command click on the line adds a dot. A single click never adds a dot. A picked dot or segment is drawn in a clearly different look (white fill or white stroke), legible on every lane colour; Shift adds to the pick; Backspace deletes picked dots in one undo step

I want to 1. be able to select a dot. 2. only add if I double click or command click, otherwise the segment is selected. 3. select segments. A selected thing should turn white or something distinct. I want to add 2 dots, select either, or select the segment in between them. this goes for any animated value on the timeline". Screenshot 2026-10-12 22.11.41: a sound's volume line with five dots; every click added one. So, for EVERY animated line on the timeline (sound volume line, key lanes, value graphs), one shared implementation: single click on a dot selects it; single click on the line between dots selects that segment; double click or Command click on the line adds a dot; a selected dot or segment is drawn distinctly (white fill or white stroke, clearly different from unselected, legible on every lane colour); Shift adds to the selection; Backspace deletes selected dots; right-click a segment for its curve. Update this task's acceptance to these rules and add a walk that: adds two dots by double click, selects each, selects the segment between them, and checks a single click never adds a dot.

USER 2026-10-13 (later, refines the earlier rule; supersedes it where they differ): "I still can not adjust the volume line in an audio clip as i expect. I click on a dot on the line, it adds another dot. I don't want to add dots by default. I want to select things. I want to add dots by cmd clicking on the line. I want to hover over a selectable thing and have it brighten a bit. I want to select a dot or segment by clicking on a dot or a segment. if a segment is selected, I want to be able to choose a different easing model somehow". Final rule for every animated line (sound volume line, key lanes, value graphs), one shared implementation: (1) a plain click NEVER adds a dot; (2) Command-click on the line adds a dot (double-click does nothing special); (3) hovering a dot or a segment brightens it a little (the shared HandleHover treatment), so the person sees what a click will take; (4) click a dot selects it, click a segment selects it, Shift adds, Backspace deletes selected dots; (5) a selected segment shows its easing and can change it: right-click the segment for the shared curve list (Linear, Ease In, Ease Out, Smooth, the rest, Hold, Draw a Curve), and the Info popover / panel shows the picked segment's Curve row; (6) selected things are drawn distinctly (white). The user is waiting on this: run these three before other work.

The shared click rule now exists (from the-value-graph task): PhotonzCore AnimatedLine (hit test: dot first within 7pt, then segment within 6pt, before/after lines are .beyond; action(for:command:shift:)) and AnimatedLinePick<KeyRef>; KeySelection now carries segments. The open graph uses it in KeyLanesView (lineSurface, graphKeyView). Gotchas found: a DragGesture never starts in a walk when the probe cannot take the front, and a plain click on a background window is swallowed while a Command-click lands; use onTapGesture(coordinateSpace:) for clicks and read modifiers from NSApp.currentEvent (KeyLaneView.clickFlags), not NSEvent.modifierFlags. Right-click menus must be built in a View body (BuiltAsItOpens) and read editorState.timelineRightPresses, or SwiftUI serves a menu built at the last redraw.

Pre-build review: a closed lane drew one bar from first to last key with no segment hit area; a clip-bar diamond's tap only moved the playhead (no pick, so Backspace would take the clip); canvas motion-path rings took no press at all. Premiere/AE: a click on a keyframe picks it, Delete removes it, a marquee picks several; AE drags a motion-path keyframe in space. Plan: closed lanes become the same AnimatedLine as the graph (flat), clip diamonds pick every key at their moment, rings pick their Position key and drag it in space.
